Latin quote (from model note, verified): «cujuscunque possibilis cum altero possibili»
English quote (anchor copied from packet text): «They consider absurd the view of those who ascribe to God countless decrees about»
ADJUDICATED @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 (Densify (agent), 2026-10-09 (Strang fix)): False positive, checked clause by clause against the Latin. (1) source_identity: 'Strangius' here is the same man Le Blanc names in full as 'Joanne Strangio' (De Decretis Pars Secunda XIX, 1675 PDF 475), i.e. John Strang of Glasgow (1584-1654), author of the cited De voluntate et actionibus Dei circa peccatum (1657); the forename identifies him consistently with the book's other renderings (§§1776-1782, 1862, 1928-1937) and corrects the earlier wrong 'William'. The note records the identification. (2) 'This includes cases where' renders 'etiam in iis in quibus' (even in those in which) - nothing added. (3) 'between any one possible thing and another' renders 'cujuscunque possibilis cum altero possibili'; 'another' takes 'possible thing' as its noun, so 'possibili' is not dropped. This entry supersedes the earlier §2033 adjudication in decretis_xxxiii_lxv_densify, whose identification ('William Strang') was wrong. GLM (glm-5.2) passed this section on every check.
